These books are a value and treasure greater than a college education in comparative mythology and religious studies ever could be. Give yourself the keys of discernment. Listen to Spirit Whirled.

recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. I have used their teas and tinctures on an almost daily basis for years now. Kyle is a great friend of InnerVerse and has appeared on the channel more times than I can count. These products work, not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

I use LotusWei Elixirs to give me an edge with psychic & energetic sensitivity, discernment, and life force coherence. In other words, LotusWei Elixirs help me be a better podcaster and Biofield Tuner. Benefits accumulate over long term use!

recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Biofield tuning and the energy field's anatomy", "body": "Chance described biofield tuning as a way of translating the messages the body gives, a modality he credited to Eileen Day McKusick. He said the energy field has a mappable anatomy, with similar information found in similar places for everyone, and that it works like the rings of a tree, so that distance from the body marks the age at which energy became stuck. Chance called the method repeatable and testable, and said he believed anyone could learn it. Mark framed the practice as an outgrowth of Chance's podcasting."}, {"title": "Symptoms as messages rather than malfunctions", "body": "Chance contrasted what he called the mainstream model of the body as a broken vehicle with his view that symptoms point to deeper patterns in belief that need to change. He said a practitioner helps people notice recurring patterns, and that in the healing arts what you do for someone else is often something you are doing for yourself. Mark agreed that healing yourself changes the reality around you, and added that others nearby may be inspired to begin their own healing journeys."}, {"title": "True will, desire, and The Neverending Story", "body": "Chance said he was not a Crowley fan but read the line about doing what thou wilt as an esoteric call to ask who you really are and what you want. He used the boy Bastion in The Neverending Story to illustrate his view that wishing for things that are not your true desire leads to forgetting who you are. Chance suggested that disconnection from real desire shows up in the energy field and in modern life, and said religions taught people to feel shame about it. Mark listened and asked follow-up questions."}, {"title": "Sacral energy, sublimation, and abundance", "body": "Chance described the sacral region of the energy field as tied to desire, fulfillment, self-worth, and flow, and said the mystery traditions practiced sublimating sexual energy into creative work. He argued that abundance depended less on positive thinking than on healthy flow of desire, summing it up as desire being the current in the river of abundance. Mark asked what Chance recommended for blockages in this area and wondered about the effect on collective consciousness. Chance presented all of this as his own interpretation from client work and personal experience."}, {"title": "Germ theory, pleomorphism, and practical tools", "body": "Chance said he doubted germ theory, and argued that bacteria change form in response to what the body needs, citing pleomorphism and what he called microzyme particles. These were his views, and he named several researchers and guests Mark might look up. He also recommended a weighted tuning fork sold through Eileen Day McKusick's store, which he said could be placed on points of the foot that correspond to organs. Chance finished by describing his AI-assisted music and pointing listeners to his website for free biofield resources."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: My friend Mark Steeves, known as Mystic Mark, had me back on his show My Family Thinks I'm Crazy to talk about my work as a biofield tuning practitioner. We covered how the energy field holds our history, why desire matters for health, and what the body is trying to tell us.
